design.title: swarmy architecture
design.description: Swarmy control plane and persistent computer model. Placement leases and epochs fence one hosting node per agent; background upload and periodic snapshots establish disk durability. Node, snapshot, and collector flows describe the target for subsequent tasks.

containers.label: Messaging
containers.description: NATS carries work between services and live output to observers. It never holds the truth about a session.

containers.label: Agent computers
containers.description: Long-lived computers hosted under placement leases; local process state is lost on rebuild.

containers.label: Control plane
containers.description: Stateless processes. Any number of each can run, and any of them can be killed and restarted at any time.

containers.label: Durable state
containers.description: The truth about every session. Services hold nothing between steps.

nodes.label: Credential file
nodes.description: The Codex-compatible auth.json holding the ChatGPT id, access, and refresh tokens. Refreshes are serialized per account and written atomically with owner-only permissions.

nodes.label: swarmy-chaos
nodes.description: The slice 1 acceptance program: starts schedulers, workers, and gateways, drives many sessions concurrently, kills random processes, and checks every log for exactly one request per step and the expected final answer.

nodes.label: ChatGPT backend
nodes.description: The Codex backend's Responses endpoint, called with a subscription access token and account id and answered as a server-sent event stream. The fake provider stands in for it in tests.

nodes.label: swarmy CLI
nodes.description: swarmy run creates a session, appends the prompt, wakes it through the scheduler, and streams live output until the session is idle. swarmy session show and list read the durable log. swarmy auth login and import manage ChatGPT credentials.

nodes.label: Garbage collector
nodes.description: Planned collector: trace live heads, last ten snapshots, clones, images, and pinned checkpoints. Recheck references and coordinate with publication before deleting objects after a grace window.

nodes.label: FoundationDB
nodes.description: The source of truth: session records, append-only event logs with contiguous sequence numbers, leases with an expiry index, the runnable index, idempotency records, in-flight inference records, and snapshot pointers. Values above 80 KiB are replaced by blob pointers.

nodes.label: Inference gateway
nodes.description: Consumes inference jobs for one provider class. Claims the request's idempotency record, streams the model response, publishes every delta live, then commits the completion, clears the in-flight record, and sets the session Runnable in one transaction before acknowledging.

nodes.label: NATS JetStream
nodes.description: Four work queue streams (inference jobs, runnable nudges, remote tools, node tools) as durable pull consumers whose acknowledgement deadline acts as a delivery lease, plus core NATS subjects for live session events, model deltas, and the scheduler wake request-reply.

nodes.label: Node agent (swarmyd)
nodes.description: Hosts long-lived computers with registered capacity. Renews placement leases, fences tools by epoch, stages dirty chunks continuously, and checkpoints before eviction after thirty idle minutes.

nodes.label: Object storage
nodes.description: Content-addressed volume chunks and manifests, retained disk snapshots, harness snapshots, and large event payloads. SeaweedFS in local development.

nodes.label: Placement record
nodes.description: FoundationDB record per agent: node id, epoch, lease expiry, last change reason and time. Atomic capacity reservation and fenced takeover after expiry. Epoch counter survives release.

nodes.label: Scheduler
nodes.description: Owns a set of the 256 runnable partitions. Scans the runnable index and publishes a nudge per due session, resending after an interval. Reaps expired leases back to Runnable. Serves wake requests over NATS request-reply.

nodes.label: Snapshot loop
nodes.description: Planned node loop: publish a clean disk snapshot every ten minutes, keep the last ten, and support explicit checkpoint. Publication checks both placement epoch and writer lease.

nodes.label: Step worker
nodes.description: Consumes nudges for its partitions, claims the session lease, loads the harness snapshot and event tail, runs one harness step, executes local tools such as get_time, and either submits an inference job or ends the turn. Renews the lease while working and holds nothing between steps.

notes.text: Twenty sessions, five steps, fifteen kills: passes with provider calls within steps plus gateway kills.
Killed mid-stream, the job is redelivered; the idempotency record makes the retry cost at most one extra provider call, never a lost session.
At-least-once delivery only. Every consumer re-checks FoundationDB before acting.
Local development runs SeaweedFS from scripts/dev-stack.sh.
One step per claim: BuildInference, DispatchTools, FoldResults, or EndTurn. Killed mid-step, the lease expires and another worker replays the same step safely.
